newsitem.title: USA: Video questioning of tobacco execs due in April.
newsitem.headline: Video questioning of tobacco execs due in April.

text.p: Videotaped questioning of leading tobacco company executives will begin April 15 in New York, a plaintiffs' lawyer in two Florida class-action suits against cigarette companies said on Monday.

The chief executive of Lorillard, a unit of Loew's Corp, will be questioned by anti-tobacco lawyers on April 15, and the heads of Philip Morris USA, a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc and the RJR Tobacco subsidiary of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp holdings will be questioned on April 17.

Plaintiffs' lawyer Stanley Rosenblatt said in an interview after a court hearing that the chief executive of Brown & Williamson, a unit of Britain's B.A.T Industries Plc, will be questioned on April 18.

Rosenblatt, pressing two class-action suits against tobacco companies which are scheduled for trial later in 1997, won the right to question the executives in recent weeks. All four have been named to their posts within the last few years.

Rosenblatt has said the videotaped questioning may be used in the trials, one involving the claims of non-smoking flight attendants allegedly injured by second-hand smoke on passenger jets. It is scheduled to begin on June 2.
